The auto tech major’s IPO plans came to light in January 2026 after cofounder and CEO Chopra said that Cars24 would list on the bourses in the next six to twelve months (July 2026 to January 2027). 

However, in September 2026, Cars24 CFO Shivanshu Makkar reportedly said that the used-car marketplace would be able to complete its reverse flip from Singapore to India only by April 2027. It will then file its DRHP for an IPO.

If the plan materialises, Cars24 would become the second auto tech startup to go public, after rival CarTrade. 

On the financial front, Cars24’s operating revenue jumped 25% to ₹6,917.1 Cr in FY24 compared to ₹5,529.6 Cr in the year ago fiscal. Net losses also rose 7% to ₹498.4 Cr from ₹467.7 Cr in FY23.

Flipkart

Founded in 2007 by Binny Bansal and Sachin Bansal, Flipkart has grown from a small online bookstore into India’s largest ecommerce marketplace. Walmart acquired majority control in the ecommerce juggernaut in 2018 for $16 Bn. Since then, it has also expanded into fintech, travel tech and quick commerce.

Flipkart was last valued at $35 Bn after a $1 Bn fundraise in 2024. Arguably the biggest startup in the country by valuation, the decacorn received in-principle approval from a Singapore court in September 2025 to reverse flip back to India for its IPO. The plan was then cleared by the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) in December 2025.

Subsequently, the company redomiciled back to India in March 2026 after receiving the nod from the Indian government. A month later, reports surfaced that the ecommerce major was exploring raising a pre-IPO round of $2 Bn to $2.5 Bn from Indian and foreign investors. 

Taking a sharp U-Turn in May 2026, reports surfaced that Flipkart had deferred its IPO till at least 2028 to focus on profitability before its public listing. This came after parent Walmart directed the ecommerce company to focus on achieving EBITDA breakeven in FY27 itself.

The ecommerce major’s B2C arm, Flipkart Internet Private Ltd, reported an operating revenue of ₹20,493 Cr in FY25, up from ₹17,907 Cr in FY24. Meanwhile, losses also narrowed 37% to ₹1,494 Cr from ₹2,359 Cr, showing improved unit economics despite diversification.

Furlenco

Founded in 2012 by Ajith Mohan Karimpana, Furlenco operates a furniture and appliance rental platform across 28 cities like Bengaluru, Mumbai, Delhi NCR, Chennai, and Kolkata. With over 300 SKUs, the platform also sells new furniture.

Backed by Sheela Foam, Lightbox Ventures, Crescent Ventures, and White Oak, Furlenco has raised more than $290 Mn to date.

In September 2026, reports surfaced that the furniture and appliance rental startup had kicked off proceedings for a potential ₹1,000-1,200 Cr public issue. Furlenco is said to be close to appointing ICICI Securities as an advisor for its IPO, which will target a valuation of around ₹7,000 Cr. Furlenco is looking to launch the IPO in FY28.

The furniture rental startup turned profitable in FY25, with a net profit of ₹3.1 Cr as against a net loss of ₹130.2 Cr in FY24. Meanwhile, its revenue from operations spiked 64% to ₹228.7 Cr in the fiscal under review from ₹139.6 Cr in FY24.

GoBoult

Founded in 2017 by Varun Gupta and Tarun Gupta, GoBoult (formerly Boult) is a smart wearables brand that sells a range of earbuds, smartwatches, neckbands and speakers. The company rebranded to a new name in August 2025 following a trademark infringement case filed by its rival boAt.

The bootstrapped startup competes with the likes of boAt, Noise and Pebble. GoBoult sells its products via its own website, online marketplaces, quick commerce platforms as well as 3,000 offline stores across India.

Kicking off its IPO plans, GoBoult cofounder Varun Gupta told Inc42 that the smart wearables brand is planning to file its DRHP with SEBI by November 2026. The company is eyeing a listing on the bourses by the summer of 2027. 

On the financial front, GoBoult reported an operating revenue of ₹762.9 Cr in FY25, up 9.4% from ₹697.2 Cr in the previous fiscal year. Its profit stood at ₹24.2 Cr during the fiscal, a near 10X jump from ₹2.5 Cr reported in FY24. 

Imarticus Learning

Founded in 2012 by Nikhil Barshikar and Sonya Hooja, Imarticus Learning is an edtech platform that offers upskilling programs in finance, digital marketing, data analytics, GenAI, and others to individual learners and corporate employees.

The platform claims to have trained nearly 40,000 learners across B2C and B2B verticals. Backed by Global Ivy Ventures, Capian, and BLinC Invest, Imarticus has raised over $11.7 Mn to date.

In April 2025, cofounder and CEO Barshikar told Inc42 the company was looking to file its DRHP with SEBI for a ₹750 Cr IPO, which would comprise both fresh issue of shares and an OFS. At the time, the edtech company could be staring at a valuation of ₹5,000 Cr to ₹6,000 Cr. 

After more than a year of suspense, reports once again surfaced in October 2026 that the startup was looking to file its DRHP with SEBI via the confidential pre-filing route by January 2027. Imarticus is now said to be eyeing a ₹1,000 Cr IPO.

On the financial front, Imarticus Learning’s revenue grew over 16% to ₹159 Cr in FY24 from ₹136.8 Cr in FY23, as per Tofler. Net losses, however, shot up nearly 10% to ₹24.6 Cr from ₹22.4 Cr in the year ago fiscal.

InMobi

Founded in 2007 by Naveen Tewari, Piyush Shah, Mohit Saxena and Abhay Singhal, InMobi is an adtech platform that offers a suite of product discovery and monetisation tools.

Based in Singapore, the SaaS company also maintains offices in Bengaluru, New York, Beijing,  and Dubai. With investments from Sherpalo Ventures, SoftBank, Kleiner Perkins, and others, InMobi has secured over $320 Mn in funding to date and was one of India’s earliest unicorns back in 2011.

Last heard, the startup was planning to file its DRHP with SEBI for a potential $1 Bn listing at a valuation of $8 Bn to $10 Bn. In July 2026, reports surfaced that the adtech unicorn had roped in four merchant bankers, namely JPMorgan Chase, Jefferies, Kotak Mahindra Capital and Axis Capital, to helm its upcoming $1 Bn (₹9,634 Cr) public issue.

However, this will not be InMobi’s first stab at an IPO. In 2021, it was reportedly planning for an IPO but shelved the plans due to adverse market conditions and funding winter.

Leverage Edu

Founded in 2017 by Akshay Chaturvedi, Leverage Edu is a study abroad platform that helps students apply to foreign universities. Its horizontal stack also spans offerings like fintech, accommodation, travel and career support. 

Besides its core app, it also offers test preparation courses for exams like IELTS and TOEFL. 

The startup claims to have so far catered to more than 1.75 Lakh customers. Leverage Edu has so far raised nearly $73 Mn from names such as Blume Ventures, DSG Consumer Partners, and Kaizenvest.

In April 2026, Inc42 reported that Leverage Edu had begun discussions with both domestic and international investment bankers for an IPO. The startup is looking to raise ₹2,000 Cr to ₹3,000 Cr via its public issue, which will comprise both fresh issue of shares and an OFS component. The platform is eyeing a valuation of over $900 Mn. 

In September 2026, Inc42 reported that the startup was looking to raise a ₹500 Cr as part of a pre-IPO round. Sources further added that the company is in the process of finalising merchant bankers for its public issue and will file its DRHP with SEBI by 2027-end.

On the financial front, Leverage Edu’s revenue from operations zoomed 91% to ₹173 Cr in FY25 from ₹90.6 Cr in the year-ago fiscal. In line with the top line, losses also rose nearly 56% to ₹106 Cr from ₹68 Cr in FY25. 

Mohalla Tech (ShareChat)

Founded in 2015 by IIT Kanpur alumni Ankush Sachdeva, Bhanu Pratap Singh and Farid Ahsan, Mohalla Tech operates social media platform ShareChat, short video platform Moj and subscription-based microdrama app QuickTV.

It has raised over $1.2 Bn in funding till date from names such as Lightspeed, Tiger Global, Temasek, Tencent, among others.

Kicking off its IPO plans, Mohalla Tech cofounder and CFO, Manohar Charan, told a publication that the startup is targeting a public listing to raise over $400 Mn in the next four to five quarters (FY28). 

On the financial front, ShareChat managed to narrow its adjusted EBITDA loss by 72% to ₹219 Cr in FY25 from ₹793 Cr a year ago. However, its operating revenue remained nearly flat at ₹723 Cr as against ₹718 Cr in FY24.

Navi                                                              

Founded in 2018 by Flipkart cofounder Bansal and Ankit Agarwal, Navi is a fintech startup that offers a range of financial services such as loans, digital payments, insurance, and mutual fund investments.

Reports in February 2025 first indicated that Navi was likely eyeing a public listing in the second half of FY26. However, the startup later deferred its IPO plans. 

Subsequently in August 2026, reports once again surfaced that Navi was planning to file its DRHP with SEBI by December 2026, eyeing a fresh issue-only IPO of about ₹3,000 Cr. The fintech unicorn is also said to have appointed JM Financial, Kotak Mahindra Capital, Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan as advisers for the proposed offering. 

Ahead of the IPO, Dutch VC giant Prosus in August 2026 also invested $100 Mn in the fintech startup, marking the latter’s first institutional capital raise.

This isn’t Navi’s first attempt at going public. It first filed a DRHP with SEBI in 2022 for an  ₹3,350 Cr offering but scrapped the plan amid market turbulence.

On the financial front, Navi’s net loss widened 268.7% to ₹465.99 in FY26 from ₹126.4 Cr in the prior fiscal year. This came despite operating revenue increasing 16.8% to ₹2,981.7 Cr from ₹2,565 Cr in FY25.

OfBusiness

Founded in 2015 by Asish Mohapatra, Ruchi Kalra, Bhuvan Gupta, Chandranshu Sinha, Nitin Jain, Srinath Ramakkrushnan and Vasant Sridhar, OfBusiness runs a B2B ecommerce platform that sells construction materials and offers financing solutions to customers.

In November 2024, the startup roped in five investment banks, namely Axis Capital, Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, Citigroup, and Bank of America, to helm its IPO. Right after, CFO Bhavesh Keswani revealed plans for a $750 Mn to $1 Bn public issue. However, the plan did not materialise. 

Reviving its IPO plans two years later, reports once again surfaced in August 2026 that the B2B ecommerce unicorn was looking to file its DRHP with SEBI by November 2026. This time, it is eyeing a $800 Mn IPO, which could comprise a fresh issue of up to $260 Mn and a $540 Mn OFS. OfBusiness is said to be targeting a valuation in the range of $5-6 Bn.

On the financial front, the B2B ecommerce giant reported a 21% jump in its consolidated profit to ₹724 Cr in FY26 from ₹597 Cr in FY25. However, operating revenue remained largely flat YoY at ₹20,645 Cr. 

PayNearby

Founded in 2016 by Anand Kumar Bajaj and Yashwant Lodha Subhash Kumar, PayNearby utilises its network of local retail shop owners to facilitate digital financial services for its customers. Its offerings include cash withdrawals, remittances, bill payments, deposits, and insurance.

The fintech startup claims to have more than 12 Lakh retail partners under its belt and has raised nearly $4 Mn in funding to date.

Kicking off its IPO preparations, cofounder and CEO Bajaj shared in August 2025 that PayNearby is eyeing a FY27 listing. The company is also finalising a merchant banker as it looks to file its DRHP with the SEBI soon.

PayNearby’s standalone operating revenue slipped 4% to ₹355 Cr in FY24 from ₹368 Cr in the year ago fiscal. Meanwhile, profits fell 25% to ₹1.5 Cr from ₹2 Cr in FY23.

PayU India

Prosus-backed payments solutions provider PayU India’s IPO ambitions remain on hold. In June 2025, the Dutch giant announced it was deferring the listing to first strengthen its operations.

This was the third time that the company delayed its IPO plans. Early 2025 reports had suggested that PayU was gearing up to file its DRHP for a post-Q1 FY26 markets debut, but the plans failed to materialise.

Earlier in November 2023, Prosus’ then CIO Ervin Tu had projected readiness for a H2 2024 listing via a $500 Mn IPO. That plan also fizzled. 

The June 2025 postponement of the IPO followed a ₹1,013 Cr rights issue from parent Prosus in April 2025. Notably, a few months later in September, reports once again surfaced that the fintech major was looking to raise $250 Mn to $300 Mn in a pre-IPO round to broaden its investor base, test demand, and set a benchmark valuation for the listing.

As per parent Prosus’ annual report, PayU India’s revenue climbed 21% to $669 Mn in FY25 from $551 Mn in the year ago fiscal. The investor also claimed that PayU’s India payment arm broke even in H2 FY25  while adjusted earnings before interest and taxes (aEBIT) margin improved by 1 percentage point to -2% in the financial year under review.

Practo

Founded in 2008 by Shashank ND and Abhinav Lal, Practo helps patients book appointments with doctors for online consultations, order medicines, and book diagnostic tests. It also offers software solutions for doctors, clinics, and hospitals. The startup also operates 40 co-branded dermatology clinics across the country.

The health tech startup has raised nearly $230 Mn in funding to date from the likes of Tencent, Peak XV Partners (then Sequoia Capital), Z47 Partners (erstwhile Matrix Partners India), Sofina, among others. 

Practo was initially planning to list on the Indian bourses in 2026 but has now moved the IPO timeline to 2027. Ahead of the listing, in February 2026, reports surfaced that the startup was in advanced talks to raise up to $125 Mn in a pre-IPO round, in a mix of equity and debt, at a valuation of $700 Mn. 

The startup reported an operating EBITDA of ₹15 Cr on a revenue of ₹234 Cr in FY25. 

Rebel Foods

Founded in 2011 by Kallol Banerjee and Jaydeep Barman, Rebel Foods is a cloud kitchen unicorn that operates multiple quick service restaurant (QSR) brands such as Behrouz Biryani, Ovenstory Pizza, The Good Bowl, SLAY Coffee, Wendy’s, among others. 

The startup has so far amassed over $563 Mn in funding from the likes of Coatue Management, Lightbox, Peak XV Partners, and Temasek. The startup was last pegged at $1.4 Bn during its last $25 Mn fundraise from Qatar Investment Authority in April 2025. 

The company’s IPO plans first came to light in October 2024 after reports surfaced that Rebel Foods was looking to list on the bourses in the next 18 months (April 2026). However, the company is yet to even file its DRHP. 

However, in a major top-level rejig in July 2025, the company’s cofounder and India CEO Ankush Grover was appointed as global CEO, while incumbent Jaydeep Barman was elevated to the role of chairman and group CEO.

On the financial front, the unicorn’s net losses shrank 12% to ₹336.6 Cr in FY25 from ₹380.3 Cr in the year ago fiscal. Meanwhile, operating revenues grew 14% to ₹1,617.4 Cr from ₹1,420.2 Cr in FY24.

Servify

Founded in 2015 by Sreevathsa Prabhakar, Servify is a B2B device management platform that offers protection plans, buybacks, and exchanges. The startup earns a majority of its revenue from sale of services such as device protection plans and platform licences.

Besides India, it also operates in the US, Canada, China and the Middle East. The startup has raised nearly $130 Mn in funding to date from BEENext, Blume Ventures, DMI Sparkle Fund, Iron Pillars, and others.

Inc42 exclusively reported in January 2025 that the Mumbai-based startup had enlisted three investment bankers for a $400 Mn to $500 Mn IPO at a likely valuation of $1.5 Bn. The offering will likely lean heavily on OFS (55-60%), with the remaining 40-45% reserved for fresh issue of shares. 

Servify was previously looking to list on the exchanges by Q1 2026, but the plan looks far-fetched as the company is yet to even file its draft IPO papers with the markets regulator. 

Meanwhile, Servify saw hefty improvement on the financial front in FY24 as loss shrank 59% YoY to ₹93.81 Cr. This came largely on the back of operating revenue increasing 23% YoY to ₹754 Cr in the fiscal under review. 

Spinny

Founded in 2015 by Niraj Singh, Mohit Gupta, and Ganesh Pawar, Spinny operates a full-stack marketplace that enables users to buy and sell certified used cars. Unlike aggregators, the platform owns the inventory and refurbishes cars in-house.

Backed by marquee names such as Fidelity, Accel, Tiger Global, General Catalyst and WestBridge Capital, the startup has raised more than $784 Mn in funding to date. It was last valued at around $1.5 Bn during its $170 Mn fundraise, which was a mix of primary and secondary deals, in early-2026.

It competes with the likes of CARS24, CarDekho, and Droom in India’s growing used car market.

Kicking off its IPO proceedings, Spinny, in April 2026, roped in Kotak Mahindra Capital, Morgan Stanley, and Citigroup as bankers for its potential IPO. 

In September 2026, the startup pre-filed its DRHP with SEBI via the confidential route. The Gurugram-based startup is looking to raise ₹2,500 Cr to ₹3,000 Cr through a combination of fresh issue and an OFS component. It is targeting a potential listing in 2027.

On the financial front, Spinny’s net loss declined 28% to ₹423.8 Cr in FY25 from ₹590.3 Cr in the previous fiscal year. Operating revenue rose 25% to ₹4,656.1 Cr in the fiscal under review from ₹3,730 Cr in FY24.

Square Yards

Founded in 2014 by husband-wife duo Tanuj Shori and Kanika Gupta Shori, Square Yards runs a full-stack proptech platform for property search, property management tools, and home interior financing.

The startup has raised more than $200 Mn in funding from Reliance Group, ADM Capital, Bennett Coleman & Co Ltd (BCCL), Genkai Capital, and others.

In May 2026, Square Yards’ CFO Piyush Bothra told Inc42 that the company was looking to rope in bankers to explore a $250-300 Mn IPO in the next 12 months. 

If the IPO materialises, Square Yards will be among a handful of Indian startups where founders will continue to hold more than 50% stake. 

On the financial front, the proptech startup clocked an operating revenue of ₹2,086 Cr in FY26 on a gross profit of ₹476 Cr.

Udaan

Founded in 2016 by Vaibhav Gupta, Sujeet Kumar and Amod Malviya, Udaan operates a B2B-focused ecommerce platform. Operating across categories like FMCG, staples and fruits & vegetables, the platform also facilitates supply chain and logistics solutions for retailers. 

It also has a fintech platform called udaanCapital, which offers financial services to small businesses and helps them with their working capital requirements. 

Backed by marquee names such as Lightspeed, DST Global, Altimeter Capital and Tencent, Udaan has raised more than $2.17 Bn in funding to date.

In March 2026, Udaan’s cofounder and CEO Vaibhav Gupta told a publication that the company was eyeing a listing on the Indian bourses in the next nine to 18 months. Gupta added that the B2B ecommerce major plans to commence the process of redomiciling back to India from Singapore “soon”.

On the financial front, Udaan reported a 37% YoY decline in net loss to ₹1,055 Cr in FY25, while operating revenue also declined 20% YoY to ₹4,561 Cr during the fiscal under review.

Wonderchef

Founded in 2009 by celebrity chef Sanjeev Kapoor and Ravi Saxena, Wonderchef sells a range of kitchenware and home appliances such as coffee machine, mixer grinders, cast iron pans, among others. 

The startup sells its offerings via its own website, ecommerce platforms as well as its own exclusive business outlets (EBOs). Backed by the likes of Sixth Sense Ventures, Amicus Capital, Godrej Family Office, Malpani Group, among others, the brand has raised more than $30 Mn in funding to date. 

The D2C brand was mulling filing its DRHP with SEBI for an OFS-heavy IPO at a likely valuation of ₹1,800 Cr. This is double compared to Wonderchef’s last-known valuation of ₹900 Cr. 

The D2C brand’s net profit soared 300% to ₹6 Cr in FY25 as against a profit of ₹1.6 Cr in the year ago fiscal. Revenue from operations jumped 13.9% to ₹430 Cr in the fiscal under review from ₹377.7 Cr in FY24.

Zypp Electric

Founded in 2017 by Akash Gupta and Tushar Mehta, Zypp offers EV-based mobility solutions for delivery workers. Besides the core EV leasing business, it also operates EV battery swapping, maintenance and servicing infrastructure.

It also runs an advertising business and has developed a fleet management software platform, called Fleekies.ai.

Backed by the likes of Japan’s ENEOS Group, 100Unicorns, Anthill Ventures and Venture Catalysts, the EV logistics startup has raised more than $75 Mn in funding to date.

In June 2026, cofounder and CEO Gupta told Inc42 that Zypp Electric has roped in Axis Capital, SBI Capital Markets and DAM Capital to manage its upcoming public offering. He said the startup is looking to raise up to $200 Mn (about ₹1,890 Cr) via its IPO within the next 18 to 24 months. 

Ahead of the listing, Zypp Electric is looking to raise a pre-IPO round in the range of $40-50 Mn from private equity firms and impact-focused funds. 

On the financial front, Zypp Electric’s revenue from operations zoomed 49% to ₹438 Cr in FY25 from ₹293 Cr in the previous year. Meanwhile, net loss widened 20.1% to ₹107.5 Cr from ₹89.5 Cr in FY24.

item.title: Meesho’s Next Monetisation Engines
item.dc:creator: Gargi Sarkar
item.description: Meesho has spent much of its journey building scale in India’s value commerce market. Its low-cost marketplace model has helped…
item.content:encoded:
Meesho has spent much of its journey building scale in India’s value commerce market. Its low-cost marketplace model has helped it expand its reach beyond large cities, bring more sellers online and attract consumers looking for affordable products. But as the company moves towards its next phase of growth, the goalpost is shifting from acquiring users and expanding transactions to extracting more value from the ecosystem it has built.

Advertising is emerging as one of the key opportunities. With 284 Mn annual transacting users (ATUs) and 1.13 Mn annual transacting sellers as of Q2 FY27, Meesho has a large marketplace that it can potentially monetise through sponsored listings and other advertising products. The company expects advertising to become a more meaningful contributor to its revenue mix from FY28.

At the same time, Meesho is exploring newer business lines, including lending products for consumers and sellers, while expanding branded commerce through Meesho Mall and discovery-led shopping through content commerce. These initiatives could open up additional revenue streams, although their contribution to the company’s financials remains at an early stage.

The opportunity comes as Meesho makes progress on its marketplace economics. 

Its Q2 FY27 performance shows that the core marketplace is growing and its operating economics are improving. Revenue from operations increased 34% year-on-year to ₹4,119.9 Cr, while net merchandise value (NMV) grew 23% to ₹12,911 Cr. 

In the reported quarter, its contribution margin improved to 6% of net merchandise value (NMV), compared with 4.6% in the previous quarter and 3.3% a year earlier. Its marketplace adjusted EBITDA loss also narrowed to ₹130.5 Cr from ₹371 Cr in Q2 FY26. 

However, management cautioned that the 6% contribution margin recorded in Q2 FY27 should not be viewed as the new normal, as some of the logistics efficiency gains may be passed on to consumers and sellers to support growth.

The question, therefore, is whether Meesho can turn its growing consumer and seller base into higher-value revenue streams without compromising the affordability that underpins its marketplace.

Advertising: Can Meesho Monetise Its Scale?

Advertising offers Meesho a way to generate more revenue from the traffic and transactions already flowing through its platform. As its user base and seller ecosystem expand, the company has an opportunity to charge sellers for better visibility and access to consumers who are actively browsing products.

For sellers, sponsored placements can help products stand out in a crowded marketplace. For Meesho, they can create an additional revenue stream without requiring it to take ownership of inventory or significantly change its core marketplace model. This is particularly relevant in a business where affordability and low prices remain central to customer acquisition.

The scale of the opportunity is supported by Meesho’s operating metrics. Its ATUs grew 21% year-on-year to 284 Mn in Q2 FY27, while annual transacting sellers increased 60% to 1.13 Mn. Placed orders rose 17% to 819 Mn during the quarter, and NMV grew 23% to ₹12,911 Cr.

“A larger marketplace gives Meesho more opportunities to connect seller advertising with consumer discovery. However, the size of its user base alone does not determine how much it can earn from ads. The company will need to demonstrate that sellers are willing to spend consistently on advertising and that paid placements generate measurable returns through product views and orders,” an ecommerce analyst said.

Advertising monetisation is still at a relatively early stage. On the Q2 FY27 earnings call, it said the sequential improvement in contribution margin was primarily driven by logistics efficiencies, rather than a significant increase in advertising monetisation. It also expects advertising to become a more meaningful contributor as a percentage of NMV in FY28.

Motilal Oswal expects higher advertising monetisation to support contribution margin expansion from FY28, citing seller demand for advertising and the potential to improve the platform’s monetisation.

However, Meesho will have to balance monetisation with the shopping experience. Its value-commerce positioning depends on offering consumers affordable products and a wide selection. If sponsored placements make discovery less relevant or push sellers towards higher advertising expenditure that is eventually reflected in product prices, the company could risk weakening some of the advantages of its model.

The other consideration is the distribution of advertising benefits across sellers. Larger and more established sellers may have greater capacity to spend on visibility, while smaller sellers could find it harder to compete for prominent placements. Meesho will need to build an advertising ecosystem that delivers returns for sellers across different sizes and categories, the analyst added..

The key monitorable, therefore, is not simply the growth in advertising revenue, but how much of that revenue Meesho can retain as incremental contribution after accounting for the cost of serving the marketplace. If advertising can scale without materially increasing operating costs or affecting affordability, it could become a more durable margin lever.

New Initiatives: Lending, Mall And Content Commerce 

Beyond advertising, Meesho is looking to deepen its engagement with consumers and sellers through a wider set of services. These initiatives could increase the number of ways in which the company earns from its ecosystem, although they are at different stages of development.

One area is lending. During the earnings call, management confirmed that Meesho is working on both consumer-side and seller-side lending products. The company is expanding its network of non-banking financial company (NBFC) partners and is also looking to work with banks.

For consumers, access to credit could potentially support purchases on the platform, while seller financing could help merchants manage working capital and grow their businesses. If structured effectively, these offerings could strengthen Meesho’s relationship with both sides of the marketplace.

However, the company has not disclosed lending-related assets under management, revenue targets or the expected financial contribution of these products. It is also not clear how much of the lending opportunity Meesho intends to capture directly versus through its lending partners. For now, it is better viewed as an emerging business opportunity than an established monetisation engine.

Meesho Mall and content commerce represent another route to deepen marketplace engagement. Meesho Mall, which had around 1,800 brands in Q2 FY27, recorded 81% YoY growth in NMV. NMV from Tier 3 and smaller markets grew 89%, while around half of Mall customers during the quarter were first-time buyers on the branded-commerce offering.

The growth indicates that Meesho is making progress in bringing branded products to a consumer base that has traditionally been associated with unbranded and lower-priced merchandise. A broader product mix could help the platform attract new customer segments and increase the range of purchases made by existing users.

Content commerce is also expanding. Its NMV grew 160% YoY in Q2 FY27, while the number of content pieces generating orders increased 144% to 2.2 Mn. The ecosystem had more than 4 lakh sellers participating in content-led commerce.

The proposition is to use videos and other content formats to help consumers discover products, rather than relying entirely on search-led shopping. This could create more product discovery opportunities and potentially improve engagement. Meesho has also said that the share of orders coming from discovery-led recommendations has increased, alongside time spent on the platform.

However, rapid growth from these offerings does not automatically translate into a meaningful revenue contribution. Meesho has not disclosed the share of total NMV generated by Mall or Content Commerce, nor has it provided specific monetisation targets for either. Their longer-term value will depend on whether they can increase purchase frequency, attract higher-value transactions and create additional opportunities for advertising.

AI is another part of this effort. Meesho is using AI across product discovery, ranking, fraud prevention and logistics, while also deploying AI agents in engineering and other internal functions. The company said 65% of its engineering pods were operating with one engineer directing AI agents. It reported a 41% reduction in code-review approval time and a reduction in data-science model deployment time from 17 days to three days.

These productivity gains could help the company develop products and improve operations faster. But AI also brings infrastructure costs. Meesho’s GPU footprint increased 150%, while server costs rose to 2.3% of NMV in Q2 FY27 from 1.9% in the previous quarter. Management expects these costs to normalise towards the previous baseline as a percentage of NMV by Q4 FY27, but that remains an expectation to be tested.

The newer initiatives are also still investment-heavy. Management has indicated that it is keeping investments in these businesses within a cap of around ₹200 Cr, while emphasising that product-market fit and unit economics will be important before scaling further. This suggests that Meesho is not yet positioning these offerings as immediate contributors to profitability.

The Profitability Test

The monetisation opportunity has to be seen alongside Meesho’s broader effort to improve its marketplace economics. The company reported a contribution margin of ₹775 Cr in Q2 FY27, up from ₹531 Cr in Q1 FY27. As a percentage of NMV, the margin improved to 6% from 4.6% sequentially.

The improvement was largely driven by lower logistics costs, supported by better order density, network redesign, improved route utilisation and efforts to reduce return-to-origin (RTO) orders. Management also indicated that it intends to recover some of the logistics-related margin spread lost in FY26 towards FY25 levels during FY27.

However, it has cautioned against extrapolating the Q2 contribution margin as the new normal. Some of the savings could be passed on to sellers and consumers through lower prices, while a part may be retained to improve profitability. The timing and extent of this balance will matter as Meesho enters the festive period and continues to invest in growth.

There are also costs that could absorb some of the gains. Meesho’s advertising and sales promotion expenses increased ahead of the festive season, taking growth spending to 2.9% of NMV in Q2 FY27 from 2.1% in Q1. Server costs also rose, reflecting the higher computing requirements of the platform.

The company reported a consolidated adjusted EBITDA loss of ₹172.1 Cr in Q2 FY27, while its consolidated net loss narrowed to ₹132.4 Cr from ₹411.4 Cr a year earlier. Although the marketplace business is moving towards better unit economics, its newer initiatives continue to add to the overall loss.

Cash flow also needs to be viewed over a longer period. Meesho reported positive consolidated free cash flow of ₹345 Cr in Q2 FY27, compared with an outflow of ₹226 Cr in Q1. But its last-twelve-month consolidated free cash flow remained negative at ₹565 Cr. The quarterly improvement was partly supported by seasonal working-capital movements, as collections from consumers ahead of the festive sale preceded settlements with sellers.

This makes the quality and durability of cash generation an important measure of progress. Advertising could help improve margins because it allows Meesho to monetise marketplace activity without taking on inventory. Lending and other initiatives may create additional revenue opportunities, but their economics will depend on partner arrangements, customer adoption and the cost of scaling.

Brokerage views reflect both the opportunity and the execution risks. Motilal Oswal sees advertising as a medium-term margin lever and expects contribution margins to remain well above FY26 levels. Nomura, however, has flagged the possibility of some margin improvement reversing in Q3 FY27 as the company reinvests gains into growth and category expansion during the festive season.

Ultimately, Meesho’s next phase will depend on how effectively it monetises the scale it has already built and whether new businesses can add revenue and improve customer and seller engagement without pushing up costs or weakening Meesho’s low-price proposition. For a platform that has built its position on affordability and scale, monetisation will have to deepen the business without changing what makes it attractive to consumers and sellers.

item.title: Netflix Flips Its India Script
item.dc:creator: Gargi Sarkar
item.description: What if Netflix’s next big hit in India is not an expensive scripted original, but a reality show with a…
item.content:encoded:
What if Netflix’s next big hit in India is not an expensive scripted original, but a reality show with a ready-made fan base? The streaming giant appears to be warming up to an idea it once seemed determined to move away from: television.

Netflix is increasingly turning to established television franchises, reality formats and non-fiction programming to reach a wider audience in India. Its recent content choices, including Lock Upp, The Great Indian Kapil Show and deals for MTV Hustle and MTV Roadies, point to that shift in India.

The change is significant for a platform that initially built its India proposition around premium, urban-focused originals and international programming. In the fourth quarter of 2021, Netflix cofounder and the then CEO Reed Hastings described India as a “frustrating” market. He also stated that the company had not managed to get its flywheel spinning here as it had in other major markets.

Nearly five years later, Netflix emerged stronger. In the July-September quarter of 2026, its India revenue grew 18% year-on-year (YoY) on a foreign-exchange-neutral basis, while viewing hours increased 24%. The company also recorded its largest-ever quarter of paid net additions in the country.

The growth was driven by a content lineup featuring Lock Upp, Netflix’s first daily reality series, as well as scripted titles such as Musafir Cafe and Operation Safed Sagar. Netflix said Lock Upp generated the highest viewing hours of any title on its platform in India, measured over the first 91 days.

So, was this simply a strong quarter or evidence of a more fundamental shift in Netflix’s India playbook? 

Netflix Looks Beyond Its Urban Comfort Zone

Netflix’s growing interest in reality television is becoming difficult to miss. The platform has even bought MTV Roadies to Netflix India in a deal worth around ₹18 Cr with JioStar, as per media reports. And the strategy is not limited to one show. 

Over the past year, non-fiction content has assumed greater importance in Netflix’s strategy. This is also part of a larger effort to move beyond its Tier I, urban-centric audience. 

According to an industry analyst at one of the Big Four consulting firms, if Netflix wants to deepen its penetration and crack the Indian market, it cannot continue catering largely to the same urban viewers. It needs formats and stories that resonate with audiences across smaller cities and towns as well.

Reality and unscripted formats could help bridge that gap. Lock Upp’s performance on Netflix offers an early indication of the format’s potential. 

Regional programming is another part of this effort. Netflix is working with local production houses and regional OTT players to deepen its presence in language markets. Netflix has partnered with Bengali streaming platform Hoichoi to bring its upcoming series to a wider audience. Under the two-year deal, the shows will premiere in Bengali on Hoichoi and also be available on Netflix in Hindi, Tamil and Telugu.

Going All In On Bollywood Blockbusters

Netflix has continued to expand its film catalogue by securing streaming rights to established Bollywood titles and major theatrical releases. Its partnership with Yash Raj Films (YRF), announced last year, is one example. 

The deal brought a curated selection of YRF films to Netflix in phases, including nine Shah Rukh Khan films such as Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge, Mohabbatein and Veer-Zaara, along with Salman Khan blockbusters Ek Tha Tiger, Sultan and Tiger Zinda Hai. The lineup also included classics such as Chandni and Silsila, and Ranveer Singh films including Band Baaja Baaraat and Gunday.

The strategy extends beyond catalogue licensing to recent theatrical releases. Netflix also picked up the streaming rights to Dhurandhar, which landed on the platform in January 2026 following its release in theatres. For its sequel, Dhurandhar: The Revenge, Netflix secured international streaming rights, while JioHotstar acquired the India rights. 

An Ormax Media analysis of 126 films that crossed one million domestic footfalls in 2025 found that Netflix held a 36% share of streaming rights across the titles, the highest among platforms. Its share in Hindi theatrical films stood at 57%, up from 50% in 2024. 

The Race To Grab Eyeballs Gets Fiercer

Netflix’s India strategy is taking shape against the backdrop of an increasingly crowded streaming market. According to JustWatch’s Q2 2026 report, Netflix and Amazon Prime Video were tied at the top, each accounting for 22% of measured consumer interest. 

Netflix is also seeing stronger traction on the ground. In Q3 2026, the company recorded its highest-ever quarterly paid net additions in India, crediting a strong local content slate and its first transaction-based loyalty bundle with Flipkart. The partnership gives Netflix another route to consumers beyond direct subscriptions, tapping into Flipkart’s existing commerce ecosystem.

Its competitors, meanwhile, are not sitting still. Amazon Prime Video is doubling down on Indian intellectual property, multilingual programming and established franchises, while also looking to take Indian stories to global audiences. At its 2026 content showcase, the platform unveiled nearly 55 Indian original series and films, with more than 100 projects in development or production.

JioHotstar, on the other hand, is banking on a combination of television content, live sports, originals and regional programming to hold on to its mass-market audience. In January 2026, it introduced monthly subscription plans across its Mobile, Super and Premium tiers, starting at ₹79, making access more flexible for smartphone viewers and connected-TV households.

Apple TV+ is also widening its distribution reach. After gaining four percentage points in JustWatch’s rankings over the past year, it has expanded its India offering through an iCloud+ subscription bundle that combines access to Apple TV and Apple Arcade with cloud storage.

But audience growth is only one part of the equation. 

Netflix’s financial performance in India offers another measure of its progress. Netflix Entertainment Services India LLP reported a 63% increase in net profit to ₹85 Cr in FY25, while revenue from operations grew 32% to ₹3,769 Cr, according to filings with the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.

The cost of that growth, however, remains significant. Total expenses rose 32% to ₹3,711 Cr during the year. Other expenses, which include content production, marketing and related operating costs, increased 35% to ₹3,616 Cr, while personnel costs declined to ₹88 Cr from ₹106 Cr.

With content and related operating expenses accounting for most of its cost base, the company will need to ensure that its investments in new formats, wider audiences and distribution partnerships translate into sustained revenue growth and stronger returns on content spending.

Can It Go Mass Without Losing Its Edge?

Netflix’s position in India’s content market also varies across language industries. The South Indian film market is more fragmented, with producers having multiple streaming platforms to sell their content to, giving them greater bargaining power. On the other hand, the Hindi film industry has become more dependent on Netflix, according to industry sources. 

For Netflix, however, the bigger challenge is balancing audience expansion with its premium content positioning. Its growing focus on reality shows, established television franchises and mass-market formats could help it reach viewers beyond its traditional urban audience. 

But moving too far towards familiar, broad-appeal programming also carries the risk of diluting the distinctive content proposition that helped build Netflix. The platform will need to widen its audience without losing the storytelling ambition and premium identity that set it apart from other streaming services. 

This tension was also evident when Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos questioned, on Nikhil Kamath’s podcast, whether the platform had introduced Sacred Games too early in its India journey. His remarks irked sections of India’s creative community, which raises concerns over whether Netflix’s evolving strategy could come at the cost of the creative ambition that defined its early India slate.

That balancing act will be central to Netflix’s next phase of growth in India. Reality shows and established television franchises can bring in viewers who may not have been drawn to its earlier slate of premium scripted originals. Regional partnerships can deepen its presence across language markets, while distribution tie-ups can make subscriptions more accessible. However, the early growth signals need to translate into sustained engagement and subscriber additions for the strategy to deliver lasting results.

One strong quarter, even with record paid net additions, does not necessarily mean Netflix has cracked India. The company continues to face competition from Prime Video and JioHotstar, alongside a growing number of platforms competing for viewers, content and production partnerships. Can Netflix turn its new mass-market appeal into a lasting winning formula without losing its DNA? 

[Edited by Shishir Parasher]

item.title: Here’s Why Doctors Are Betting On Docterz’s Hospital Management Software
item.dc:creator: Palak Sharma
item.description: Running a clinic involves more than examining patients. Like any business, doctors also need to manage their schedules, patient records,…
item.content:encoded:
Running a clinic involves more than examining patients. Like any business, doctors also need to manage their schedules, patient records, billing, staff and follow-ups, leaving them with less time to focus on medical care.

Mumbai-based Docterz is building a platform to ease this administrative burden. Founded over a decade ago by practising paediatrician Dr Atish Laddad, the startup offers an integrated electronic medical records and clinic management platform for doctors, clinics and healthcare organisations. It aims to simplify day-to-day clinic operations while helping doctors deliver more accessible and affordable healthcare.

With AI opening up new possibilities for automating routine tasks and improving clinical workflows, Docterz is looking to deepen its technology offering for the medical community.

The healthtech startup has now raised ₹5 Cr from around 35 investors, nearly 60% of which, or close to ₹3 Cr, came from approximately 20 doctors who already use its platform. The investor group also includes Sugar Cosmetics’ Vineeta Singh and CaratLane’s Avnish Anand.

The fresh capital will be used to drive organic growth, explore acquisitions and develop practical AI-powered tools for doctors.

Bringing Clinical And Administrative Workflows Under One Roof

In essence, Docterz aims to reduce the administrative workload of running a clinic, allowing doctors to spend more time on patient care while giving them better control over their clinic’s operations.

From arranging appointments and maintaining records to then aiding in prescriptions, billing, the all-in-one clinic management platform helps doctors handle everything. For this, the platform trains AI based OS on doctors’ prescription patterns to simplify the process of recommendations.

It also provides easy-to-understand medical information that doctors can share with patients, alongside tools to manage vaccine inventory, track expiry dates and monitor the use of medical supplies.

On the patients side, Docterz offers a WhatsApp-based assistant to book appointments, check live clinic waiting times, access medical records and view appointment history without downloading a separate app.

Docterz’s Commercial Bet

The latest fundraise comes with an interesting investor mix. Nearly 60% of the capital has come from doctors who already use Docterz, making the round a bet by its own customer base on the startup’s future.

According to the startup, several of these doctors have used the platform for years. For instance, Dr Dhananjay Sangle, a paediatrician and one of the user-investors, said he had been using Docterz across his clinic’s paediatric and OB-GYN practices for several years.

The participation of existing users could give Docterz an advantage as it looks to expand within the medical community. However, scaling a healthcare software business will require it to convert this initial user trust into wider adoption across independent practitioners and healthcare organisations.

With its users also now present on its cap table, the startup’s next phase of growth will focus on three areas:

  • AI-enabled tools: Docterz plans to introduce practical AI capabilities to address everyday clinical and practice-management tasks, including documentation, administrative workflows and practice-data analysis.
  • Organic and inorganic expansion: The company intends to grow its existing business while exploring acquisitions and other inorganic opportunities.
  • Wider doctor adoption: Docterz plans to reach more independent practitioners and smaller clinics across India, while continuing to build its patient-engagement capabilities.

It also plans to strengthen integrations with India’s digital-health ecosystem, including the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM).

Inc42 Take: Can Docterz Become The Operating System For Doctors?

Docterz is targeting a fairly fundamental problem in healthcare.

An integrated platform could help reduce a doctor’s burden, particularly for independent practitioners and smaller clinics that may not have the resources to manage multiple systems.

The participation of around 20 existing doctor-users in the round is also an encouraging signal of product acceptance. However, user trust is only one part of building a scalable healthcare software business.

The larger challenge now is to get more doctors to move their existing records and workflows onto the platform. Once they are there, their retention also depends on whether the software can deliver tangible operational benefits.

AI could also open another avenue for growth, particularly across documentation, patient follow-ups and administrative tasks. 

The value of these tools will depend on how seamlessly they fit into doctors’ existing workflows and how responsibly patient information is handled.

item.title: ED Arrests Armstrong Exchange Founder Over Alleged Online Betting Scam
item.dc:creator: Gaurav Bagur
item.description: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has arrested Armstrong Exchange founder Sagar Dash in connection with an alleged online gaming and betting…
item.content:encoded:
The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has arrested Armstrong Exchange founder Sagar Dash in connection with an alleged online gaming and betting scam.

In a statement, ED said that Dash was arrested on October 27 under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002. A special PMLA court in Mumbai has now remanded Dash to ED custody for three days.

The directorate said that the probe was initiated after three FIRs were filed in connection with online betting and cyber fraud involving All Panel Exchange (APX). Afterwards, the ED began probing the operations of APX and related financial transactions. 

The agency subsequently uncovered an alleged network of mule accounts and shell entities, which were used to route proceeds of crime worth hundreds of crores.

The agency alleged that Dash used fabricated documents and KYC details of an account, maintained on behalf of an entity called Armstrong Exchange Pvt Ltd and set up by Dash, with Nagarbhavi Credit Cooperative Society to open a cryptocurrency account. 

The ED further claimed that hundreds of crores were routed through the cooperative society’s bank account, with a substantial portion directly linked to proceeds generated through illegal gaming and betting platforms.

According to the ED, the proceeds of the crime were initially routed through multiple mule accounts maintained with Jubilee Hills Mercantile Cooperative Bank in Hyderabad. The money was then transferred to various shell entities, and significant amounts were moved to the aforementioned nodal account at Nagarbhavi Credit Cooperative Society in Bengaluru.

The ED said it is continuing its investigation in the matter to trace the alleged financial network and identify other entities involved in routing the proceeds of crime.

The latest arrest follows searches conducted by the ED across Pune, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, and Surat and Mehsana in Gujarat, which resulted in the seizure of incriminating documents and the freezing of nearly ₹9 Cr in cash held across multiple bank accounts.

The agency had also arrested Ram U Ramdhani, CEO of Edsom Fintech Pvt Ltd, in connection with the probe.

The arrest is part of ED’s broader clampdown on money laundering. Just days ago, the directorate launched investigations into alleged FEMA violations involving crypto platforms Mudrex and Saber.money as well as decentralised finance (DeFi) protocol Instadapp and its associated platform, Fluid, over alleged unauthorised cross-border fund transfers worth more than ₹4,940 Cr.

Prior to this in June this year, the ED had also searched six premises linked to five platforms, namely Transak, Carret, Xpat, Onramp.money and Onmeta, over alleged unauthorised cross-border crypto transfers.

item.title: IPO-Bound StockGro’s FY26 Profit Jumps 3.3X YoY To ₹113 Cr, Revenue Doubles
item.dc:creator: Anne Florentyna
item.description: StockGro-parent AssetGro Fintech Ltd net profit for the fiscal year FY26 jumped threefold while its operating revenue doubled year-on-year.  The…
item.content:encoded:
StockGro-parent AssetGro Fintech Ltd net profit for the fiscal year FY26 jumped threefold while its operating revenue doubled year-on-year. 

The company, which filed for an IPO confidentially earlier this month,net profit surged 226.6% to ₹113 Cr during the reported year, compared to ₹34.6 Cr in FY25, according to its consolidated financial statement.

It reported a profit before tax (PBT) of ₹99 Cr in the fiscal, up from ₹35.9 Cr in FY25. However, it reported a net tax credit of ₹14 Cr, comprising a deferred tax credit of ₹15.9 Cr and a current tax expense of ₹1.9 Cr. This catapulted its profit after tax to ₹113 Cr.

The IPO-bound company reported an operating revenue of ₹226.1 Cr in the fiscal, about double of ₹113.3 Cr in the previous year.

A majority of 99.9% of its operating revenue comes from subscription fees and the remaining is from service fees.

Including other income of ₹4.8 Cr, the company’s total income stood at ₹230.9 Cr in FY26, compared to ₹125.5 Cr a year earlier.

AssetGro’s EBITDA stood at approximately ₹118.7 Cr in FY26, compared to ₹59.5 Cr a year ago, marking a growth of around 99.3%.

The growth comes amid India’s expanding retail investment ecosystem, which reached 13.66 Cr unique NSE-registered investors as of September, the company said. This presents StockGro with opportunities to expand its user base while increasing paid subscription adoption among existing users.

Incorporated in 2020, StockGro operates a platform that allows users to research, learn and invest in stocks and alternative assets. The platform combines market research with a social layer, allowing users to track stocks, study portfolios, follow other investors and interact with market experts. 

It also offers users research and trade ideas from SEBI-registered analysts, along with tools for deeper analysis. Its AI-powered research assistant Stoxo helps users analyse stocks, markets, mutual funds and other investment themes.

The investment advisory company pre-filed its draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) with the SEBI back in September. StockGro is looking to raise up to ₹2,000-2,500 Cr via the IPO, which could include a fresh issue of around ₹800 Cr and an offer for sale (OFS) by existing shareholders. 

Recently, StockGro raised ₹110 Cr (around $10.4 Mn) as a part of its ongoing Series B round, from existing investor BITKRAFT Ventures, along with Aditum Venture Capital Fund, India SME Growth Fund, and actor Suniel Shetty.

Magnifying StockGro’s FY26 Expenses

On the expenditure front, the company’s total expenses increased 47.3% to ₹132 Cr in FY26 from ₹89.6 Cr in the previous fiscal. Here is a breakdown of the total expenses:

  • Employee Benefit Expenses: Constituting half of the total expenses, employee expenses emerged as the largest cost component, increasing 96.3% to ₹65.8 Cr in FY26 from ₹33.5 Cr in the previous fiscal.
  • Technology Charges: Spending under this head rose 34.6% to ₹17.9 Cr in the year under review, compared to ₹13.3 Cr in FY25.
  • Media And Advertising: Costs under this category stood at ₹23.2 Cr in FY26, marking a 61.1% increase from ₹14.4 Cr a year ago.

item.title: New-Age Tech Stocks Gain This Week Led By Ather & Zetwerk, CarTrade Sinks 22%
item.dc:creator: Akshit Pushkarna
item.description: New-age tech stocks largely advanced this week, with quarterly earnings driving sharp moves in individual counters. Of the 69 stocks…
item.content:encoded:
New-age tech stocks largely advanced this week, with quarterly earnings driving sharp moves in individual counters. Of the 69 stocks under Inc42’s coverage, 40 gained between 0.2% and 26.8%, while the remaining 29 declined by up to 22.3%.

Ather Energy led the gainers after reporting its maiden quarterly net profit. The stock rose 26.8% to close at ₹1,755.05, having touched a fresh all-time high of ₹1,782.05 during the week.

Recently listed Zetwerk followed with an 18% gain, while Tonbo Imaging rose 15.3%. Besides Ather, Nykaa, Eternal, and Shadowfax touched fresh 52-week highs.

However, 15 stocks, including Swiggy, FirstCry, MapmyIndia, and LEAP India, hit fresh lows during the week.

Gains in larger companies helped lift the combined market cap of the 69 stocks to $160.94 Bn, up 5.7%, or $8.62 Bn, from $152.32 Bn at the end of the previous week.

Here are some key developments from listed new-age tech companies during the week.
ESDS’ CTO Resigns: AI cloud provider ESDS’ chief technology officer and chief information officer Sajiv Nair resigned, citing personal reasons. He will leave the company on or before January 27, 2027.

Nazara Funds Acquisition Tranche: Nazara Technologies infused $77 Mn into its UK subsidiary, Nazara UK, to fund the second tranche of its acquisition of Spanish gaming companies Bluetile Games and Bestplay Systems. Nazara UK paid the amount to the sellers, taking the total consideration paid to $303.02 Mn.

Zelio Adds Manufacturing Capacity: Zelio E-Mobility began commercial operations at its new Haryana plant, adding annual capacity of 72,000 vehicles, comprising 48,000 electric two-wheelers and 24,000 electric three-wheelers. It invested over ₹20 Cr in the facility, primarily towards backward integration, under its approved capex plan.

E2E Expands AI Infrastructure: E2E Networks expanded its AI infrastructure capacity by 5.4 MW, or 58.7%, to approximately 14.6 MW. The expansion will include NVIDIA HGX B300 systems and other Blackwell GPUs for AI model training, fine-tuning, and enterprise inference.

GlobalBees Raises JW Brands Stake: FirstCry’s subsidiary GlobalBees Brands acquired an additional 14.2% stake in watch and jewellery brand owner JW Brands for ₹18.7 Cr in cash, increasing its holding from 75.1% to 89.3%. JW Brands, which operates Joker & Witch, Bewitched, and Teejh, reported turnover of ₹105.5 Cr in FY26, up 8.4% from ₹97.3 Cr in FY25.

Markets Recover, FIIs Turn Buyers

The Sensex gained 1.8% this week to close at 74,459.53, while the Nifty 50 rose 2% to 23,053.10, recovering most of the previous week’s losses.

The benchmarks opened the week higher, consolidated over the next two sessions, and recovered sharply on Thursday, when the Sensex gained over 900 points. Buying continued yesterday, helping the Nifty close above 23,000.

Softer crude oil prices and easing bond yields initially supported risk appetite, according to Geojit’s research head Vinod Nair. However, renewed West Asia tensions pushed crude higher towards the weekend, prompting profit booking in the broader market.

Quarterly earnings also drove stock-specific moves, with strong results from select large companies supporting sentiment despite mixed performances across sectors.

Global monetary policy remained another focus. The US Federal Reserve held its benchmark interest rate at 3.75%-4%, although two members favoured a 25-basis-point increase. Nair said the Fed, ECB, and Bank of Japan’s continued caution on inflation tempered expectations of early monetary easing.

FIIs turned net buyers of Indian equities worth ₹6,305 Cr during the week, ending a 10-week selling streak, according to Bajaj Broking’s deputy vice president of research Pabitro Mukherjee. They bought shares in three of the five trading sessions, supporting the market recovery.

DIIs remained net buyers for the 11th consecutive week, purchasing ₹3,110 Cr of equities, although their buying moderated from ₹10,942 Cr in the preceding week.

The reversal in foreign flows followed a prolonged sell-off. A recent research report by JM Financial noted that FIIs had sold approximately $64 Bn worth of Indian equities over the 24 months through October 2026.

The brokerage argued that attractive valuations alone may not draw foreign investors back, identifying crude prices as a key influence. Its analysis associated Brent crude above $105 a barrel with FII selling, while prices below $90 coincided with a more favourable flow environment.

Investors will track next week’s US midterm elections, Brent prices, developments in the US-Iran and Russia-Ukraine conflicts, and quarterly earnings, Mukherjee said.

CarTrade Falls After Earnings

CarTrade shares declined 22.3% this week to close at ₹2,189.95 after its September-quarter results fell short of brokerage expectations despite revenue and EBITDA growth.

The automotive classifieds company’s consolidated net profit rose 3% YoY to ₹66 Cr, while operating revenue increased 10.2% to ₹213.1 Cr in Q2 FY27. EBITDA grew 20% to ₹76 Cr, with its margin expanding to 36% from 33% a year earlier.

However, JM Financial flagged slowing growth in the core consumer business, which includes CarWale, BikeWale, and CarTrade. Its revenue increased 4% YoY to ₹79.5 Cr, compared with growth of 18% in Q1 FY27 and 25% in Q4 FY26, and was 12.4% below the brokerage’s estimate.

OLX India’s revenue grew 26.4% to ₹70.2 Cr but missed JM Financial’s estimate by 9.7%. Meanwhile, monthly unique visitors across the consumer business fell 17.9% YoY and 8.5% QoQ to about 43 Mn. The brokerage flagged concerns over traffic growth and the potential impact of AI on classifieds platforms.

JM Financial downgraded CarTrade to ‘ADD’ from ‘BUY’ and cut its 12-month price target by 25.4% to ₹2,650 from ₹3,550. It lowered its FY27-FY29 revenue estimates by 3%-6% and EBITDA estimates by 8%-13%.

Ather Rallies After Turning Profitable

Ather Energy shares gained 26.8% this week to close at ₹1,755.05 after the electric two-wheeler maker reported its maiden quarterly net profit in Q2 FY27.

Its consolidated net profit stood at ₹1.3 Cr against loss of ₹154.1 Cr a year earlier and ₹51.1 Cr in Q1 FY27. Operating revenue increased 62.9% YoY to ₹1,464.2 Cr.

EBITDA stood at ₹74.2 Cr, with its margin improving to 4.9% from negative 9.6% a year earlier. However, other income of ₹62.7 Cr remained crucial to the bottom line, with operating revenue falling ₹61.5 Cr short of total expenses.

Sales rose 42% YoY to 93,211 units, customer enquiries increased 109% to around 10 Lakh, and pre-orders more than doubled to 1.8 Lakh. CEO Tarun Mehta said supply constraints persisted, with internal estimates indicating potential sales of around 20,000 units a month were going unrealised.

Ather plans to invest ₹122 Cr to add 2.25 Lakh units of annual manufacturing capacity across its Hosur and upcoming AURIC facilities. This would take combined installed capacity to about 11.4 Lakh units by Q2 FY28.

item.dc:creator: Anjali Jain
item.description: India’s electric two-wheeler (E2W) registrations rose 2.9% to 2,14,654 units in October from 2,08,688 units in September, with TVS Motor…
item.content:encoded:
India’s electric two-wheeler (E2W) registrations rose 2.9% to 2,14,654 units in October from 2,08,688 units in September, with TVS Motor and Hero MotoCorp gaining market share.

According to Vahan data as of 16:00 IST today, registrations increased for the second consecutive month, although growth slowed from September’s rebound.

Inc42 had reported a 12.2% MoM increase to 2.07 Lakh registrations in September, based on data available on October 1. The latest figures put September registrations at 2,08,688 units, implying 13% growth over August’s revised tally of 1,84,671 units.

October registrations rose 48.1% YoY from 1,44,980 units a year earlier. The month also recorded the highest registrations in the October 2025-October 2026 period covered by the data.



However, performance varied across manufacturers. TVS and Hero MotoCorp recorded gains, while Bajaj Auto, Ather Energy, and Ola Electric saw registrations decline. 

TVS Leads, Hero Gains

TVS retained the top spot, with registrations rising 7.4% to 58,425 units from 54,399 units in September. Its market share increased to 27.2% from 26.1%.

Bajaj Auto remained second despite a 4.3% decline in registrations to 46,658 units from 48,740 units. Its market share fell to 21.7% from 23.4%.

Hero MotoCorp recorded the strongest growth among the top five manufacturers. Its registrations jumped 17.5% MoM to 28,720 units, lifting its market share to 13.4% from 11.7%.

This narrowed its registration gap with third-placed Ather Energy to 1,660 units from 6,507 units in September. Ather’s registrations declined 1.8% to 30,380 units from 30,942 units in September, while its market share slipped to 14.2% from 14.8%.

Manufacturers Plan Capacity Expansion

The registration declines at Ather and Bajaj came amid capacity constraints flagged by both companies.

Ather said it estimates missing out on around 20,000 potential retail sales a month because of supply constraints. Its customer pre-orders more than doubled to around 1.8 Lakh during the September quarter, equivalent to approximately 60,000 a month, against average monthly production of around 33,000 units.

The company said its Hosur facility reached 98% capacity utilisation during peak production in Q2 FY27. It plans to add 2.25 Lakh units of annual production capacity across its facilities by Q2 FY28, taking combined installed capacity to around 11.4 Lakh units.

Bajaj Auto also flagged capacity constraints across its EV businesses. CFO Dinesh Thapar said during the company’s earnings call that manufacturing limitations meant it could deliver only 75% of its planned volumes.

The company plans to increase monthly Chetak production capacity to approximately 80,000 units by Q4 FY27 from 64,000 units currently.

Meanwhile, TVS announced plans in October to increase E2W production to 80,000 units a month by March 2027.

Ola Electric’s Registrations Decline Further

Ola Electric’s registrations fell 13.7% to 11,614 units in October from 13,458 units in September. Its market share dropped to 5.4% from 6.4%.

The decline comes amid the company’s efforts to revive its sales and distribution network, alongside its push into more affordable products and in-house battery technology. Yesterday, it closed its ₹1,000 Cr rights issue.

Among smaller manufacturers, Greaves Electric Mobility’s registrations increased 12.3% MoM to 10,468 units, while River recorded a 15.7% rise to 6,533 units.

E-Sprinto’s registration growth moderated to 6.4% MoM in October from over 1,500% in September. It registered 2,124 units during the month.

The company also launched its G1 family electric scooter in October, marking its entry into the B2C segment. Deliveries are scheduled to begin on January 1, 2027, with the company targeting sales of around 5,000 G1 units by March 2027.

item.title: [Update] Forensic Audit Finds External Breach Behind €3 Mn Capillary Fraud
item.dc:creator: Anjali Jain
item.description: Update | October 31, 19:33 IST A forensic audit by KPMG has found that the €3.04 Mn banking fraud at…
item.content:encoded:
Update | October 31, 19:33 IST

A forensic audit by KPMG has found that the €3.04 Mn banking fraud at Capillary Technologies’ subsidiary SessionM Czech Republic was most consistent with an external payment-diversion scam involving impersonation of a senior executive and an external lawyer.

Capillary, in an exchange filing today, said the fraud likely involved a lookalike email domain, social engineering and communications through WhatsApp and personal email accounts.

The investigation found no evidence of malware, unauthorised access, mailbox compromise, account takeover or traditional email spoofing in the systems and records examined. It also did not identify any evidence of employee involvement. However, the audit could neither establish nor rule out the use of deepfake audio or video, as original recordings, mobile-device data and call records were unavailable.

Of the four disputed transactions, three payments went to ZZDJB CO LIMITED at HSBC Hong Kong, while the fourth was transferred to ZHONGXIAN TRADING PTE. LTD at UOB Singapore.

While the investigation established the initial transfers, it did not trace the subsequent movement of funds, identify the ultimate beneficiaries or assess the prospects of recovery. It also could not independently verify the company’s payment approval processes due to missing bank-portal and workflow records.

KPMG concluded that the incident was primarily a social-engineering-led fraud. Capillary said it has strengthened payment controls and is pursuing recovery efforts and legal remedies.

Update| July 31, 15:15 IST

Days after it announced a cyber fraud of €3 Mn (about ₹32.7 Cr) at one of its step-down subsidiaries, SaaS company Capillary Technologies said it has initiated a forensic audit to investigate the suspected fraudulent and unauthorised banking transactions.

The audit, approved by the company’s Audit Committee, will be conducted by KPMG Assurance and Consulting Services LLP and will examine the transactions, banking processes, internal financial controls, identify the root cause and recommend corrective measures.

“The forensic audit has been initiated with a view to independently examine the facts and circumstances relating to the incident, determine the root cause and recommend appropriate corrective measures,” the company said in its exchange filing. 

Original | July 6, 17: 41 IST

SaaS company Capillary Technologies announced that one of its “recently acquired step-down subsidiaries” has been hit by a cyber-enabled banking fraud, leading to a loss of €3 Mn (about ₹32.7 Cr).

The funds were fraudulently transferred to an unauthorised third-party bank account using advanced deepfake methods including cloning, signature forging, social engineering to impersonate the company’s senior management, Capillary said in an exchange filing. As per the company, the exploit took place just prior to this weekend (before July 3).

Capillary has taken legal and operational measures to safeguard and recover the transferred funds, including working with law enforcement, cybercrime authorities and concerned banks. It further noted that the step-down subsidiary was insured under a cyber and crime insurance policy and the company is also evaluating the extent of insurance coverage and recoverability.

Upon identifying the attack, the company was able to recover €450K. It has also traced bank accounts suspected to be related to the fraud and asked related banks to put the accounts on hold.

“With the swift action by the Company and advice of the relevant local authorities, additional funds were traced, and those accounts have since been placed on hold by the respective banks, reducing the amount at risk. The exact amount currently on hold is yet to be determined,” the company said.

Despite the cyberfraud, Capillary believes that its customer data and the company’s technology infrastructure remains uncompromised.

The SaaS company’s most recent acquisition was global card network MasterCard’s customer engagement and loyalty platform SessionM, which it snagged in February for $20 Mn (about ₹190.7 Cr) to strengthen presence in the North American and Latin American markets.

Besides, the company also acquired Canada-based martech platform Kognitiv for an undisclosed amount last year.

On the financial front, Capillary’s net profit grew multifold to ₹43.4 Cr in Q4 FY26. Its operating revenue also jumped 25% YoY to ₹191.3 Cr in the March quarter. For the full fiscal FY26, Capillary’s profit skyrocketed 296% to ₹52.4 Cr from ₹13.3 Cr in FY25. The top line rose 23% to ₹734.6 Cr from ₹598.3 Cr in the previous fiscal.

Shares of Capillary ended today’s trading session 0.15% higher at ₹515.85.

The incident underscores the growing cybersecurity risks facing enterprises as AI becomes more advanced, highlighting the need for companies to strengthen their defences against increasingly sophisticated cyber threats. Last month, Apple’s supply chain data was reportedly exposed after sensitive supplier lists, component details and alleged images of its upcoming iPhone 18 Pro models surfaced online following a cyberattack on its contract manufacturer, Tata Electronics.

item.title: CapGrid Secures ₹50 Cr Funding To Deepen Its Manufacturing Play
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: Delhi NCR-based B2B manufacturing startup CapGrid has raised ₹50 Cr (about $5.2 Mn) in a Pre-Series B round to develop…
item.content:encoded:
Delhi NCR-based B2B manufacturing startup CapGrid has raised ₹50 Cr (about $5.2 Mn) in a Pre-Series B round to develop higher-end precision components and expand into sectors such as drone manufacturing and data centres.

The funding round values CapGrid at ₹430 Cr (about $45.3 Mn), cofounder and CEO Dheeraj Tiwari told Inc42. Led by Hero Enterprise Venture Partners, the investment arm of Sunil Munjal-led Hero Enterprise, it included primary and secondary transactions, with participation from Axilor Ventures, Anicut Capital, Nexus Venture Partners, and angels.

Part of the primary proceeds will fund R&D into higher-end engineered precision components, while the remainder will support business growth, Tiwari said. CapGrid previously raised $5 Mn in an extended Series A round led by Anicut Growth Fund.

Matching Suppliers With Orders

Founded in 2021 by Tiwari and Himanshu Raghuvanshi, CapGrid serves original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) and Tier I suppliers across automotive, consumer durables, and heavy industries.

It owns no factories. Instead, its cloud manufacturing platform coordinates component design, development, production, and delivery through third-party manufacturers. CapGrid says it uses AI and ML to match orders with suppliers and track production schedules and quality requirements.

According to the startup, its supplier partners operate at around 60% capacity. CapGrid pools orders from different OEMs to put that spare capacity to use.

Its supply chain control tower tracks sourcing, procurement, production, and deliveries, while 14 fulfilment centres across India’s major OEM clusters manage inventory and component deliveries to assembly lines.

CapGrid also offers new product development, import localisation, and value engineering, helping customers develop parts, replace imports, and improve component designs and sourcing costs.

Moving Beyond Automotive

CapGrid initially focused on automotive, tapping manufacturers’ need to source components and manage suppliers. India’s auto component industry recorded turnover of ₹7.59 Lakh Cr in FY26, up 12.7%, according to ACMA. Supplies to OEMs increased 16.3% to ₹6.52 Lakh Cr.

Having expanded beyond automotive, CapGrid now plans to enter drone manufacturing and data centres.

Tiwari said operating revenue grew around 14% to ₹240 Cr in FY26, with ₹350 Cr targeted for FY27. Its annualised revenue run rate has risen from around ₹300 Cr six months ago to ₹360-370 Cr, with ₹500 Cr the next target.

Inc42 Take: Can CapGrid Move Up The Manufacturing Value Chain?

CapGrid’s next bet is to move beyond consolidating component procurement into higher-end engineered parts. Its existing OEM relationships and supplier network give it a base to build on, but spare factory capacity alone will not establish an advantage in more complex manufacturing. It will depend on the engineering expertise CapGrid brings to component development and production.

The commercial question is whether this shift can improve the economics of its business. Operating revenue grew around 14% in FY26, while its FY27 target implies substantially faster growth. Entering drones and data centres could widen its customer base, but without margin and working-capital disclosures, it remains unclear whether more complex orders will translate into better returns.
